target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (new exported helper `isInternalCodexMessageTurn`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 6 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`
- `classifies internal-turn kinds for cross-context binding`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

---

**AI-assisted checklist**
- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description
- [x] Include a concise **Evidence** section with the most useful validation
- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does
- [ ] If you have access to Codex, run `codex review --base origin/main` locally and address the findings before asking for review — attempted, but blocked by a Codex usage limit (resets Jul 10); will re-run and address findings then
- [x] Resolve or reply to bot review conversations after you address them

target.title: feat(session-lock): opt-in diagnostics for embedded session fence takeovers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in observability for embedded-attempt **session fence takeovers**.

When a session `.jsonl` changes under a released prompt lock in a way the fence cannot explain as an owned in-process write, the controller tears the attempt down by throwing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` — which carries only the file path. Across the **10 takeover throw sites** in `attempt.session-lock.ts` there was previously **no diagnostic at all** (the file has no logger). In production this makes a takeover effectively opaque: the only way to learn *which* check tripped and *what* file state could not be reconciled was to patch the installed bundle and add logging by hand.

The gap is real. A released-prompt takeover can fire when a legitimate in-process writer (e.g. an outbound delivery-queue transcript append) races the fence window, and without the fingerprints and owned-write history it looks identical to a genuine external editor.

## What Changed

Every takeover-detection point now goes through a small `markSessionTakeover(reason, current?)` helper. **Behaviour is unchanged** — it sets the same `takeoverDetected` flag and the same error is still thrown. When `session-lock` debug logging is enabled it additionally emits one structured record:

- `reason` — which check tripped (`unexplained-session-file-change`, `owned-write-merge-rejected`, `write-lock-acquire-error`, …)
- `sessionFile`, `fenceActive`, `fenceGeneration`
- `expectedFingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` (dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs, stringified so the record survives any JSON transport)
- `ownedWriteCount` and `lastOwnedWriteGeneration`

It is gated behind `isEnabled("debug")`, so there is **zero overhead when the subsystem is not in debug**. No new env var — it uses the existing `session-lock` subsystem logger.

## Evidence

**Live diagnostic output.** Exercising a real external-append takeover (append to the session file while the prompt lock is released, then take the write lock) now emits, via the `session-lock` logger:

```
embedded session fence takeover: unexplained-session-file-change
{
  "reason": "unexplained-session-file-change",
  "sessionFile": ".../session.jsonl",
  "fenceActive": true,
  "fenceGeneration": 1,
  "expectedFingerprint": { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "19", "mtimeNs": "1783519408483846902", "ctimeNs": "1783519408483846902" },
  "currentFingerprint":  { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "63", "mtimeNs": "1783519408484811232", "ctimeNs": "1783519408484811232" },
  "ownedWriteCount": 0,
  "lastOwnedWriteGeneration": null
}
```

The record immediately tells the story: **same inode**, size grew `19 → 63` (a plain append), `ownedWriteCount: 0` — an unpublished writer advanced the file. That is exactly the signal needed to distinguish a benign in-process append (which would carry an owned-write generation) from a real external editor.

**Tests.** New `attempt.session-lock.diagnostics.test.ts`:
- emits the structured diagnostic (reason + fingerprints) on a real takeover,
- stays silent when `session-lock` debug logging is disabled (zero overhead),
- stays silent when no takeover occurs.

The full existing `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` suite (222 tests) passes unchanged, confirming the flag/throw behaviour is untouched. `oxlint` and a scoped `tsgo --noEmit` are clean on the changed files.

target.title: fix(agents): route streamProxy request through fetchWithSsrFGuard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `streamProxy` function in `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:301` issues an outgoing POST to the operator-configured `${options.proxyUrl}/api/stream` endpoint via the un-guarded global `fetch`. From openclaw's perspective the proxy URL is operator-controlled but the response body is **not** trusted: a misconfigured or hostile proxyUrl (e.g. one whose DNS A record rebinds to a private/internal IP between the lookup and the connect, or which streams an unbounded response body) currently bypasses every SSRF and byte-cap protection owned by `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. The SSE-byte guards in `proxy.ts` only run *after* the request has already been issued and the response headers received, so they cannot defend against the request itself.

This PR wraps the outgoing fetch with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in STRICT mode and locks the hostname to the operator-configured proxy URL via `policy.allowedHostnames`, so the same DNS-pin / private-network / body-cap / dispatcher seam used elsewhere in agents now applies to proxy egress. The existing `.catch(...).finally(...)` chain (timeout translation + requestAbort.clear) is preserved verbatim; the guard's `release` runs in the outer `finally` so the dispatcher and DNS-pin resources are reclaimed regardless of whether the stream terminates normally, hits an SSE-byte cap, or is aborted.

## Changes

- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:13` — add `import { fetchWithSsrFGuard, GUARDED_FETCH_MODE } from "../../infra/net/fetch-guard.js"`.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:289` — declare `let releaseGuarded: (() => Promise<void>) | undefined` in the IIFE scope so the outer `finally` can call it.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:299-336` — replace `await fetch(...)` with `await fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url, init: { method, headers, body, signal }, mode: GUARDED_FETCH_MODE.STRICT, policy: { allowedHostnames: [new URL(options.proxyUrl).hostname] }, auditContext: "proxy-stream" })`. Catch/finally chain preserved. `response = guarded.response` and `releaseGuarded = guarded.release`.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:431-436` — outer `finally` now also calls `await releaseGuarded?.()` inside its own `try/catch` so guard release failures cannot replace the primary result.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts:3` — add `createServer, type AddressInfo` import.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts:564-612` — inline test that drives the production `streamProxy` end-to-end against a real `node:http` loopback server (no `vi.stubGlobal("fetch")`), proving the guard's allowedHostnames policy accepts the operator host while DNS pin + dispatcher + post-stream release hold.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `streamProxy` now routes its POST to `${proxyUrl}/api/stream` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with hostname locked to the operator-configured proxy URL; DNS rebinding, private-network target, body-byte-cap, and timeout protections now apply to proxy egress.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts --run`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  git checkout fix/proxy-stream-ssrf-guard
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  13 passed (13)
    Start at  21:28:11
    Duration  2.55s
  ```
  - 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged (existing `vi.stubGlobal("fetch")` mocks still hit because `fetchWithSsrFGuard` falls back to `globalThis.fetch` when no `fetchImpl` is supplied, and the mock has the `.mock` shape the guard detects for hermetic test mode).
  - 1 new test (`routes the request through the SSRF guard with the operator-allowed proxy host`) drives `streamProxy` against a real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and asserts:
    - exactly one POST reached `/api/stream`,
    - `Authorization: Bearer token-abc` was forwarded,
    - the JSON body's `model.id` and `model.provider` match the input,
    - `options.headers` was scrubbed (the existing `sanitizeProxyModel` + `buildProxyRequestOptions` contract is preserved).
- **Observed result after fix**: Real loopback request flows end-to-end through the guard's pinned-dispatcher branch (no `vi.stubGlobal`), and the response is fully consumed before `releaseGuarded()` returns. Reverting either the `fetchWithSsrFGuard` wrap or the `policy.allowedHostnames` line makes the inline test fail (the guard would reject the loopback hostname as a private IP, or `sanitizeProxyModel` would leak `headers`).
- **What was not tested**: Live POST against a real proxy deployment; the proof is unit-level via the production constructor + loopback, the same shape approved for prior fetch-guard wiring PRs.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:232` (`probeHealth`) — sibling surface with the same pattern, submitted as a separate PR to keep each change XS.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts` and `src/infra/push-apns.relay.ts` — additional unguarded outgoing fetch sites identified during exploration; tracked as future SSRF-wiring PRs.

## Risk

- **Scope**: 1 prod file + 1 test file; +19 source LoC (net) + 53 test LoC.
- **Behavior**: Same outgoing request shape as before, plus 1 new `fetchWithSsrFGuard` option-object pass. `streamProxy`'s public signature, return shape, and event stream are unchanged.
- **No API/signature changes**: The change is entirely internal to `streamProxy`'s request path; downstream consumers (e.g. `buildGuardedModelFetch`) are untouched.
- **Compatibility**: All 12 pre-existing tests in `proxy.test.ts` still pass because `fetchWithSsrFGuard` falls back to `globalThis.fetch` when no `fetchImpl` is supplied, and the existing `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` mocks keep working (the guard detects them as mocked fetch and skips real DNS pinning).
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo` clean on the touched branch.
- **Sibling coordination**: Distinct file from `provider-local-service.ts`; submitted as a separate PR.

target.title: feat(android): manage skills from settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android now mirrors the relevant requested behaviors from the Web UI: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Notes

- `skills.securityVerdicts` still supports the existing passive installed-skill verdict collection.
- New explicit mode accepts at most 25 `{ slug, version, ownerHandle? }` items.
- Explicit mode skips installed-skill scanning and fetches only the requested default-ClawHub verdict batch.
- Explicit mode projects the same sanitized fields as installed-skill mode; raw `security` payloads are not exposed.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ui): keep clampText/truncateText surrogate-safe at emoji boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clampText` and `truncateText` in `ui/src/lib/format.ts` used `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` to truncate user-visible text. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji like 🎉, CJK extended characters), the resulting string contains a dangling surrogate that browsers render as U+FFFD (�).

**Affected UI surfaces (all via `clampText` / `truncateText` calls):**

| Surface | File | Impact |
|---------|------|--------|
| Markdown rendering | `ui/src/components/markdown.ts` (3 sites) | User-written markdown with emoji truncates to � |
| Command autocomplete | `ui/src/lib/chat/commands.ts` (5 sites) | Command names/descriptions with emoji show broken chars |
| Tool output preview | `ui/src/pages/chat/tool-stream.ts` | Streamed tool output truncated mid-emoji |
| Activity log preview | `ui/src/pages/activity/tool-activity.ts` | Activity feed entries with emoji show corruption |
| Skill descriptions | `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts` (2 sites) | Skill summary/description truncated at emoji |
| Exec-approval rules | `ui/src/pages/nodes/view-exec-approvals.ts` (3 sites) | Approval rule descriptions, commands, paths with emoji |

## Changes

**`ui/src/lib/format.ts`** (+2, −2):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `clampText()`: `value.slice(0, max-1)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-1)`
- `truncateText()`: `value.slice(0, max)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max)`

**`ui/src/lib/format.test.ts`** (+82):
- Add `clampText` and `truncateText` to imports
- Add `clampText surrogate-safe truncation` test suite (3 tests)
- Add `truncateText surrogate-safe truncation` test suite (3 tests)
- Each suite verifies truncation at an emoji boundary produces no dangling surrogates using `isHighSurrogate`/`isLowSurrogate` checks

## Evidence

**Unit tests (43/45 passed — 2 pre-existing locale failures unrelated to change):**

```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)  ← pre-existing locale issue
      Tests  2 failed | 43 passed (45)
```

The 2 failed tests (`forces a 12-hour clock when preference is 12`, `lets the caller override the resolved hour cycle`) are pre-existing locale-sensitive tests that expect `/PM/i` but receive Chinese‑locale output `下午07:30`. All 6 new truncation tests pass.

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] ═══ Platinum Proof: format.ts surrogate-safe truncation ═══
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] Text: 118 a + 🎉(2 units) + b = 121 UTF-16 units
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] [BEFORE] .slice(0, 119): lone surrogate? ✗ BROKEN
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] [AFTER]  sliceUtf16Safe(0, 119): lone surrogate? ✓ OK
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] clampText(..., 120): lone surrogate? ✓ OK
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] truncateText(..., 120): lone surrogate? ✓ OK

[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   🐚 RESULT: PASS (platinum)
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   Unsafe .slice() produces dangling surrogates at emoji boundary.
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   truncateUtf16Safe (and clampText/truncateText) eliminate them.
```

*Proof method: spawned a real Node.js process importing the fixed functions, tested truncation with emoji 🎉 positioned exactly at the boundary. Unsafe `.slice()` produces dangling surrogates; `truncateUtf16Safe`, `clampText`, and `truncateText` all produce clean output.*

target.title: fix(codex): keep root memory in bootstrap context
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #94295.

Native Codex currently suppresses root workspace `MEMORY.md` when memory tools are available, causing `/context` to show the file as present but injected with `0` chars. That makes sparse bootstrap memory unavailable unless the model already knows to ask memory tools for the right fact.

This PR keeps root `MEMORY.md` in the bounded workspace bootstrap prompt context and leaves memory tools available for deeper recall.

## Changes

- Stop selecting root `MEMORY.md` as a tool-routed bootstrap file for native Codex turns.
- Stop filtering root `MEMORY.md` out of `buildBootstrapContextForFiles(...)` when memory tools are present.
- Stop excluding root memory from Codex prompt-context selection.
- Update Codex app-server tests to expect nonzero `MEMORY.md` injection unless normal bootstrap budget truncation applies.
- Update the Codex harness reference, Codex harness runtime, token-use, and system-prompt docs for the new native Codex `MEMORY.md` default.

## Why

`MEMORY.md` is the sparse long-term bootstrap memory surface. It can contain ambient operating facts that the model needs before it can know which memory query to run. Tool-based recall is useful, but it should not replace bootstrap memory by default.

Related broader routing work: #83612. This PR is intentionally narrower and addresses the direct `MEMORY.md injected 0 chars` regression.

## Validation

target.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated (#101837)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #101837

`readResponseText` incorrectly marks responses as `truncated: true` when the total bytes read exactly equal `maxBytes`, even though no data was actually omitted.

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts:275`:
```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When `bytesRead === maxBytes`, the condition fires before confirming whether more data exists. The `truncated` variable was already correctly set at lines 264-268 when an overflow chunk was confirmed.

## Fix

Remove the `|| bytesRead >= maxBytes` check from line 275. If `bytesRead === maxBytes` and the stream is done, the next `reader.read()` returns `{ done: true }` → clean exit with `truncated: false`. If more data exists, the next chunk triggers the overflow logic at line 262 which correctly sets `truncated: true`.

## Evidence

- **2 files changed**: 19 insertions, 2 deletions
- **New test**: "does not mark exact-limit bounded reads as truncated" — 5-byte chunk with `maxBytes: 5` → expects `truncated: false`, reader not cancelled
- **All tests pass**: 24/24 (2 test files)

## Checklist

- [x] One PR = one issue
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] All tests pass
- [x] Link to issue in PR body

target.title: fix(config): use Object.hasOwn for own-key checks in write-prepare helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createMergePatch`, `collectChangedPaths`, and `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` in
`src/config/io.write-prepare.ts` use the `in` operator to test key membership
(`key in base`, `key in target`, `key in runtime`). The `in` operator walks the
entire prototype chain, so any property reachable through inheritance —
`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, or custom-prototype keys — is silently
treated as a config-owned key.

This produces three concrete failure modes:

1. **`createMergePatch`:** inherited keys appear in the output patch, injecting
   non-existent config fields into the write candidate.
2. **`collectChangedPaths`:** inherited keys are reported as changed paths,
   triggering spurious write-prepare work and incorrect diff sets.
3. **`projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape`:** authored source keys whose names collide
   with inherited property names are incorrectly skipped (the `!(key in runtime)`
   guard short-circuits before reaching the authored value).

## Why This Change Was Made

`Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the correct primitive for "does this specific object
have this key, ignoring its prototype chain." It is available in all Node.js versions
the project supports (Node 16.9+, present as standard since ES2022). Replacing five
`key in obj` guards with `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` closes all three failure modes in
one bounded change with no surface-area growth.

## User Impact

**Before:** config objects that inherit from a non-null prototype (e.g. objects created
with `Object.create(someProto)`, or objects whose prototype happens to carry own
properties named after config keys) produce incorrect merge patches, spurious changed-
path sets, and silently dropped authored source keys.

**After:** only the object's own keys are considered in all three helpers. Inherited
keys are ignored; authored keys whose names collide with prototype property names are
preserved correctly.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/fix-io-write-prepare-hasown`
Base: `upstream/main` (`9c08808bd7`)
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when building merge patches 1ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > preserves authored keys whose names match Object.prototype members 0ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when collecting changed paths 0ms
 ... (48 pre-existing tests also pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
   Duration  140ms
```

Three new regression tests cover each fixed function directly:

- `createMergePatch` with an object whose prototype has own properties → only own key `safe` appears in the patch
- `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` with a source key named `toString` → authored value is preserved, not skipped
- `collectChangedPaths` with prototype-bearing objects → only the own key `safe.mode` is reported as changed

### Diff summary

```
src/config/io.write-prepare.ts      |  6 +-  (5 key-in → Object.hasOwn replacements)
src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts | 54 ++  (3 new regression cases)
```

### Format check

```
$ git diff --check
(no output — clean)
```

### What was not tested

Live `openclaw configure` / `openclaw doctor --fix` round-trip against a real
`openclaw.json` file with a prototype-bearing config object. The fix is
mechanical — five identical `in` → `Object.hasOwn` substitutions — and the
three regression tests directly exercise all affected code paths. Crabbox/Testbox
remote CI was not available at submission time.

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` would see avoidable prompt-cache churn when an unmentioned room event interleaved with normal session turns.

The user-visible symptom from redacted live traces was that otherwise similar same-session turns alternated between mostly uncached prompts and much smaller cached prefixes, even though the session-level visible-reply contract was configured as automatic.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps strict room-event delivery unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual delivery and `forceMessageTool`. The change separates the prompt-facing reply delivery mode from the effective delivery mode so embedded system-prompt construction can use the session-stable mode already computed for binding facts.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

## User Impact

Room-event turns can preserve the same prompt/cache contract as the rest of the session without relaxing message-tool-only delivery. Operators should see fewer avoidable prompt-prefix cache misses when room-event turns interleave with direct or primary session turns.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Local validation:
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <10 touched files>`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-auto-reply.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` — 98 passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-embedded.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts -t 'uses prompt-stable source reply delivery mode for embedded system prompts'` — 1 passed, 70 skipped.

Not counted as validation:
- A full run of `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts` without `-t` produced no output for 120s and was terminated by the repository Vitest wrapper.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were stripped from the evidence before submission.

target.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth
target.body:
> **AI-assisted PR.** Implemented with the GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude). The author has reviewed and understands all changes; validated locally (targeted Vitest suites, `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint/oxfmt, SDK surface budget) and against a live `*.ghe.com` tenant (see Evidence). ## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Scope & Related Work Closes #102219. This PR extends the **existing bundled `github-copilot` provider** with data-residency domain support for the auth, token-exchange, and completions paths it already ships. It does **not** add a new provider, a new model catalog, or a config-schema change (it uses free-form provider params). Related: #96988 ("GHE.com Model Integration"), which was closed NOT_PLANNED and routed to ClawHub/plugin scope. That issue asked for a broader/new GHE model integration; this change is deliberately narrower: it makes the provider OpenClaw already bundles honor an allowlisted, fail-closed `*.ghe.com` tenant host so enterprise users are not locked out, without introducing new SDK provider surface. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. GHE Login / Auth pre-warm (gateway startup, 18:56:23 UTC) ``` subsystem=gateway level=INFO time=2026-07-02T18:56:23.756Z provider auth state pre-warmed in 477ms eventLoopMax=11.9ms ``` Stored GHE credential loaded and validated successfully on gateway boot. 2. Active GHE Copilot token state ``` integrationId: vscode-chat token: [REDACTED] updatedAt: 2026-07-02T21:03:31Z ← refreshed ~12 minutes ago expiresAt: 2026-07-02T21:33:31Z ← valid for ~17 more minutes expired? false ``` Standard 30-minute Copilot token TTL confirmed; token was refreshed mid-session against REDACTED.ghe.com. 3. target.title: Harden Program Manager behavioral evals and handoff safety
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Program Manager had strong static/smoke coverage but still had unproven behavioral output quality, no runtime telemetry emission path, and insufficient protection against unsafe indirect execution through configured delegation targets. This PR hardens Program Manager so it stays planning/status-only, emits non-secret telemetry through the agent event bus, rejects unsupported completion claims, and fails closed when configured delegation targets expose high-risk tools without deny/always approval posture.

## Summary
- add sectioned Program Manager behavioral live eval contracts and enforcement
- add canonical Program Manager state freshness metadata checks and telemetry validation fixtures
- implement Program Manager runtime telemetry on the `program_manager_telemetry` agent-event stream
- require handoff packets only and remove Program Manager `sessions_send` from allowed tools
- add static delegation-target safety checks for Program Manager handoffs
- include Program Manager safety, efficiency, and behavioral contracts in scheduled live eval defaults

## Evidence
- `pnpm docs:list`
- `pnpm openclaw config validate` — passed with existing version warning
- `pnpm openclaw approvals get --json` — passed; Program Manager, Judge, and Telemetry Evaluation Analyst now show `security=deny`, `ask=always`, `askFallback=deny` for exec
- `node scripts/agent-role-eval.mjs --agent program-manager --json` — passed with warning-only UNKNOWN canonical state
- `node scripts/agent-role-eval.mjs --contracts-only --json` — passed
- focused delegation-target static verification for Program Manager plus configured delegation targets — passed
- `pnpm test test/scripts/agent-role-eval.test.ts src/infra/agent-events.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` — passed, 95 tooling tests and 14 infra tests
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/lib/agent-role-evals.mjs test/scripts/agent-role-eval.test.ts src/infra/agent-events.ts src/infra/agent-events.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check -- control/docs control/state scripts/lib/agent-role-evals.mjs test/scripts/agent-role-eval.test.ts src/infra/agent-events.ts src/infra/agent-events.test.ts` — passed
- `env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm build` — passed
- live evals against `ollama/openclaw-control-qwen25-32b:latest` passed for `program-manager`, `program-manager-safety-boundary`, `program-manager-efficiency-routing`, `program-manager-full-output`, `program-manager-unsupported-completion`, `program-manager-handoff-telemetry-full`, and `program-manager-stale-work-full`

## Remaining Known Gap

Program Manager canonical state files intentionally remain `UNKNOWN` until an approved trusted truth source is provided. The static role eval correctly reports these as warning-level `program_manager_canonical_state_unknown` and does not allow real status claims from unknown state.

target.title: fix(signal): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in daemon stdio transport
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bindSignalCliOutput` in `extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts` attaches `'data'`
listeners to the long-lived `signal-cli` child process stdout and stderr, but
registers no `'error'` listener on either stream.

Node.js EventEmitter throws an unhandled `'error'` event as an uncaught
exception when no `'error'` listener is registered. If `signal-cli`'s stdout
or stderr emits `'error'` — common causes are a broken pipe after abrupt child
termination, an fd closed while data is still buffered, or a read EIO after
the child's file descriptors are torn down — the gateway process crashes.

The child `'error'` listener at `spawnSignalDaemon` line 160 only catches
spawn failures (e.g. `ENOENT`/`EACCES`); it does not cover stream-level errors
after the process has started. `child.on("exit")`/`child.on("close")` cover the
process lifecycle, but those events do not prevent a prior stream `'error'` from
being unhandled.

This fix adds an `'error'` handler to `bindSignalCliOutput` that routes the
error message to the caller-supplied `error` logger and lets the
`'exit'`/`'close'` lifecycle listeners complete the shutdown sequence as
before. This mirrors the pattern iMessage uses for its stdio RPC transport
(`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts:135-137`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The missing handler is a class-A Node.js crash path: any broken-pipe on a
stream with listeners but no `'error'` handler is fatal to the process. The fix
is a single `stream?.on("error", ...)` call in the shared binding helper, so
both stdout and stderr are covered by one change. No existing behavior is
altered: the data classifier, log routing, and process shutdown sequence are
unchanged.

`bindSignalCliOutput` is also promoted to `testApi` to allow direct regression
coverage without spawning a real `signal-cli` process.

## User Impact

**Before:** An abrupt `signal-cli` termination, broken pipe, or fd error on
stdout/stderr after process start crashes the OpenClaw gateway process with an
unhandled `Error: write EPIPE` (or similar). Users lose the entire gateway
session — all in-flight turns, pending deliveries, and open WebSocket
connections are torn down.

**After:** The stream error is logged (`signal-cli stdio error: …`) and the
normal `'exit'`/`'close'` lifecycle path handles the process shutdown. The
gateway does not crash.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/signal-daemon-stdio-stream-errors`  
Base: `upstream/main` (`c69724ef3b508eb42189d1731c1bcd85027ddb22`)  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression test (direct stream mock — no real signal-cli required)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > routes stdout 'error' events to the error callback instead of throwing 4ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > routes stderr 'error' events to the error callback instead of throwing 0ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > does not interfere with normal data events after an error 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon stdio stream error handling > is a no-op for a null stream 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon args > expands home-relative configPath before passing it to signal-cli 83ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > keeps routine signal-cli warnings out of error state 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > keeps recoverable prekey decrypt receive failures out of error state 1ms
 ✓ signal daemon log classification > still surfaces signal-cli failures as errors 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Duration  461ms
```

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `'error'` event on a `signal-cli` stdio stream must be
caught and logged, not crash the gateway process.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout, Node.js v22.22.0,
using the real `bindSignalCliOutput` export via the `testApi` surface. No live
`signal-cli` process was required; the stream is an `EventEmitter` that emits
`'error'` directly.

Exact command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";
import { testApi } from "./extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts";

const errors = [];
const stream = new EventEmitter();
testApi.bindSignalCliOutput({ stream, log: () => {}, error: (msg) => errors.push(msg) });

let threw = false;
process.once("uncaughtException", () => { threw = true; });
stream.emit("error", new Error("write EPIPE"));
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10));
console.log(JSON.stringify({ threw, errors, listener_count: stream.listenerCount("error") }));
EOF
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{"threw":false,"errors":["signal-cli stdio error: Error: write EPIPE"],"listener_count":1}
```

Observed result after fix: `threw: false` — the unhandled-exception path was
NOT triggered. The error was routed to the `errors` array by the registered
`'error'` listener. Gateway process stays alive.

What was not tested: live `signal-cli` binary with a real broken-pipe scenario
(requires a local Signal account and signal-cli install). The regression tests
and inline proof cover the entire `bindSignalCliOutput` error path without a
live binary.

### Format check

```
$ git diff --check
(no output — clean)
```

```
extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts      |  9 ++++++ (prod: 1 handler + 1 testApi export)
extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts | 55 +++++  (4 new regression cases)
2 files changed, 63 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` would see avoidable prompt-cache churn when an unmentioned room event interleaved with normal session turns.

The user-visible symptom from redacted live traces was that otherwise similar same-session turns alternated between mostly uncached prompts and much smaller cached prefixes, even though the session-level visible-reply contract was configured as automatic.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps strict room-event delivery unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual delivery and `forceMessageTool`. The change separates the prompt-facing reply delivery mode from the effective delivery mode so embedded system-prompt construction can use the session-stable mode already computed for binding facts.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

## User Impact

Room-event turns can preserve the same prompt/cache contract as the rest of the session without relaxing message-tool-only delivery. Operators should see fewer avoidable prompt-prefix cache misses when room-event turns interleave with direct or primary session turns.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Local validation:
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <10 touched files>`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-auto-reply.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` — 98 passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-embedded.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts -t 'uses prompt-stable source reply delivery mode for embedded system prompts'` — 1 passed, 70 skipped.

Not counted as validation:

## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now work through Signal-owned reply-author resolution instead of adding a shared `replyToAuthor` field to every outbound channel path. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies record the inbound Signal sender by conversation and message timestamp so later Signal sends can attach the native quote metadata.

The only core behavior change is scoped to Signal send actions: when the Signal message action receives an explicit `replyToId`, it is treated as the reply target and wins over an inline `[[reply_to:...]]` directive.

## What Changed

- Signal outbound sends: message adapter, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal inbound messages: accepted inbound messages register `{account, conversation, message timestamp} -> sender author` for Signal group native reply lookup.
- Signal reply-author lookup: new Signal helper keeps a bounded in-process author cache and uses the existing optional Signal runtime store hook when available.
- Signal message action: `replyToId` is accepted as a Signal-only alias for explicit reply targets, and explicit `replyToId` wins over inline reply directives.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` derive native quote authors as `+15551234567` and `username:alice`.
- Group Signal replies resolve the quote author from the Signal-owned author cache instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Signal inbound context tests prove a group message stores the sender author under its Signal message timestamp.
- Signal message-action tests prove `replyToId` is only treated as an alias for the Signal channel.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

target.title: feat(kimi): show code quota in usage status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Kimi Coding subscription users currently do not see quota usage in OpenClaw status surfaces. This adds Kimi quota reporting to the existing provider usage/status pipeline so `5h` and `7d` windows can be shown instead of omitting Kimi.

## Why This Change Was Made

The useful quota data is provider-specific (`/coding/v1/usages`), so the Kimi provider plugin owns the endpoint request and payload normalization while core only owns provider-id routing, summary fan-out, timeout/filtering, and status display.

This rebased version intentionally keeps the surface narrow:

- Registers `kimi` as a usage provider and maps `kimi-code` / `kimi-coding` aliases to it.
- Keeps Kimi endpoint fetch/parsing inside `extensions/kimi-coding/usage.ts` via `resolveUsageAuth` and `fetchUsageSnapshot`.
- Reuses existing Kimi auth sources (`KIMI_API_KEY`, `KIMICODE_API_KEY`, config/store resolution) instead of adding a new env precedence path.
- Does not export a provider-specific Kimi fetch helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-usage`.

## User Impact

When a Kimi API key is available from provider config/store or existing Kimi env vars, OpenClaw can fetch the Kimi Coding usage payload and display:

- `5h` from the matching limit entry, using either label-based matching or duration metadata.
- `7d` from the top-level `usage` row.

The fetcher supports both `used/limit` and `remaining/limit` shapes and returns stable usage errors for auth failures or malformed responses.

## Summary
- redact exec foreground tool-result text and structured `details.aggregated` before returning results to the agent
- redact node-host exec stdout/stderr/error output before formatting tool results

## Real behavior proof

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/exec-tool-result-redaction` at `da701a0bbf6c`, using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`. The proof used an obvious fake canary value, not a real credential.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

4. `bounds oversized pull body and cancels the stream` — sibling fix proof. Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

All 135 tests across both files pass: `stream-runtime.test.ts` 105/105, `setup.test.ts` 30/30.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test. Sibling fix in setup.ts: the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged (existing test `fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout` continues to pass).
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response or model-pull stream emits >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models; model pull progress events are <100 bytes per chunk). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
10 files changed, 271 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — auto-regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen --write`
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` — +1 row
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — +3/-3 LoC budget defaults (entrypoints 323→324, exports 10412→10416, callable 5227→5228)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block; signature widening is type-only)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block + `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature widening)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — +177 LoC (3 inline tests + Layer 3 loopback + quantitative read-out)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — +53 LoC (1 inline test for /api/pull bounded read)

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — typecheck passes (core + extensions)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 105/105 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — 30/30 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — 8/8 tests pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json <4 modified files>` — 0 lint errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` — local-only repro script passes
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passes
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` — passes (regenerated exports match entrypoints list)

## Closes / siblings

- Closes the symmetric success-body gap to `OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (8 KiB error-body bound, existing) on **both** Ollama NDJSON streaming paths: `/api/chat` (chat/tool-call) and `/api/pull` (model download).
- Same 16 MiB cap as #95218, #95420, #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #96920, #96984, #97535, #97620, #97628 (all canonical streaming success-body bounded-read PRs).
- First two extension consumers of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Subsequent extension consumers (Google SSE, future channels) can import from this SDK subpath without touching core.
- Companion SDK promotion commit bundles the helper re-export, entrypoints registration, exports sync, baseline hash regen, and docs row in one cohesive change — no consumer breaks if this PR is reverted, since the SDK seam is gated by the bound consumers in commits 2 and 3.

target.title: test: migrate diagnostics-timeline to createSuiteTempRootTracker
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` maintains a module-level `tempDirs: string[]` plus an `afterEach` drain to clean up ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp` allocations. Five sibling test-migration PRs (#98893, #98965, #98987, #98993, #99074) already replaced the same pattern with `createSuiteTempRootTracker` from `src/test-helpers/temp-dir.js`. The diagnostics-timeline file is the next candidate in that consolidation sweep: the manual array tracking adds cleanup logic to the test setup/teardown surface that is exactly what `createSuiteTempRootTracker` is built to centralize. After this PR, every shared-prefix temp dir in `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` flows through the same suite-level lifecycle (setup / make / cleanup) used by `src/infra/update-runner.test.ts`, `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`, `src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts`, `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/infra/provider-usage.auth.normalizes-keys.test.ts`, and `src/infra/device-pairing.test.ts`.

This consolidation keeps the `beforeAll/afterAll` lifecycle close to the production code, removes the chance of a forgotten `tempDirs.push`/`splice(0)` pair, and lets new tests in this file opt in to one line (`tracker.make("timeline")`) instead of re-deriving the temp-root setup.

## Changes

- `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts`: replace module-level `tempDirs: string[]` and the `afterEach` drain with `createSuiteTempRootTracker({ prefix: "openclaw-diagnostics-timeline-" })`. `setup()` runs in `beforeAll`, `cleanup()` runs in `afterAll`. `createTimelineEnv()` now calls `suiteTracker.make("timeline")` instead of `fs.mkdtemp` + manual array push. Removed `mkdtemp`, `rm`, and `tmpdir` imports (no longer needed).

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(session-fork): add 2s timeout to parent-fork token count resolution
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime` reads the parent transcript file and parses recent usage with no timeout or abort boundary. On a large transcript (hundreds of MB) or a slow filesystem (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), the async call can hang indefinitely, blocking every new thread/reply in the session and exhausting async context slots in the gateway.
- **Fix:** Wrap the entire transcript-stat + transcript-read path in a `withTimeout(2 000 ms)`. Before the timeout fires, the function accumulates a `bestEffortTokens` value (cached `totalTokens` from the store entry, then the byte-size estimate from `fs.stat`). If the deadline is exceeded the timeout error is caught and the best-effort value is returned, keeping session creation moving.
- **Out of scope:** Increasing the timeout value or making it configurable — 2 s is conservative enough for local SSDs and generous enough to survive a slow-cold read. Config surfacing can come later if needed.
- **Reviewers:** Focus on the `bestEffortTokens` mutation inside the `withTimeout` closure and whether the catch path correctly returns the last accumulated value.

## Linked context

Closes #101718

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Parent-fork token-count resolution no longer hangs when the parent transcript is unreadable within 2 seconds; session creation falls back to cached or byte-estimate token counts.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15 (Apple M-series), Node 22.19, local dev checkout (`pnpm dev` not running — unit-test-only proof; no live gateway needed for this path).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  ✓ resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime > falls back to cached parent tokens when transcript usage hangs 2ms
  ✓ resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime > keeps the byte estimate when transcript usage times out after stat succeeds 3ms
  ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > keeps forking when the runtime cannot produce a bounded parent token count 1ms

  Test Files  1 passed (1)  |  Tests  8 passed (8)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)  |  Tests  2 passed (2)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Both timeout cases resolve correctly — cached tokens returned when stat also hangs, byte estimate returned when stat succeeds before the deadline, and the fork decision degrades gracefully to `{ status: "fork", maxTokens: 100_000 }` when runtime returns `undefined`.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway session creation against a real NFS/FUSE mount; macOS CI cross-path (Linux CI is the truth target). The 2 s wall-clock timeout is covered by `vi.useFakeTimers` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** `vi.useFakeTimers` drives the timeout, so this is deterministic unit proof rather than real-clock wall-time proof. The production path (`withTimeout` from `infra/fs-safe`) uses real `setTimeout`; the unit tests confirm the branching logic is correct.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose` — 8/8 pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 pass
- Regression test added: two new tests in `session-fork.runtime.test.ts` (timeout with cached fallback; timeout with byte-estimate fallback); one new test in `session-fork.test.ts` (fork decision when runtime returns `undefined`)

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? **No** — the resolution path is internal to session-fork; the fork/skip decision exposed to callers is unchanged for the normal (non-timeout) case.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No** — no new config keys or env vars.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No**.
- Highest-risk area: the `bestEffortTokens` variable is mutated inside the async closure before `withTimeout` resolves; if `estimateParentTranscriptTokensFromBytes` throws synchronously that value stays `undefined` and the catch returns `undefined` — same as the old behavior.
- Mitigation: `estimateParentTranscriptTokensFromBytes` already has its own `try/catch` and returns `undefined` on error; the only new failure mode is the timeout path, which is tested.

## Current review state

- Next action: awaiting maintainer review
- Bot comments addressed: none yet
- AI-assisted: yes (Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6); human-run Vitest output pasted above; `codex review` not run (no local Codex binary available in this checkout).
