target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(agents): allow re-entrant session write lock for overflow-recovery compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97747: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process. `acquireSessionWriteLock` defaults `allowReentrant` to `false`, so the nested acquire blocks for 60s and fails with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`. Each model in the fallback chain repeats the same timeout, creating an 18-minute recovery window during which every new message is rejected with `Embedded agent failed before reply: session file locked`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `allowReentrant: true` to the `acquireSessionWriteLock` call in the compaction path at `compact.ts:1214`. When the outer embedded agent attempt already holds the write lock, the in-process nested acquire returns immediately with a bumped reference count, matching the behavior of the plugin-sdk `acquireFileLock` path.

## User Impact

- Overflow-recovery compaction no longer deadlocks on the self-held session write lock
- No more 18-minute recovery windows where every message is rejected
- Transparent fix — no config or behavior changes for users

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` — 50 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts` — 54 tests pass

target.title: [AI] fix(codex): strip internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Since v2026.6.9, Codex app-server runs stamp internal/heartbeat turns with `currentChannelProvider = "webchat"` (the internal message channel). The cross-context guard (`enforceCrossContextPolicy`) then denies every heartbeat notification the main agent sends to a Discord channel via the `message` tool, producing `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` The deny is silent because `heartbeat_respond` still returns success — no error is surfaced and notifications are lost.

Bisection: worked on v2026.6.8, first denial appeared after updating to v2026.6.9.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: PRs [#93813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93813) / [#94203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94203) introduced `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` in `dynamic-tool-build.ts` and wired it into `run-attempt.ts:900` and `side-question.ts:921` as `currentChannelProvider`. For Codex runs originating from the embedded backend (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts`), `messageChannel` is always `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`"webchat"`) — a fallback value for all non-channel-agent runs (heartbeat, cron, TUI, sessions_spawn). Before 6.9, `currentChannelProvider` was not set for Codex-backed runs, so the guard's provider-mismatch check was a no-op and the heartbeat `message` tool to Discord worked.

The fix: in `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider`, return `undefined` when the resolved value equals `"webchat"` (the internal channel constant). This restores the pre-6.9 behavior where Codex-backed runs carry no channel binding. Real delivery channels (discord, telegram, slack, etc.) still propagate correctly because they use their actual channel names, not the internal fallback.

## User Impact

Users with Codex-backed agents and the documented HEARTBEAT.md pattern (`message` tool → notify a Discord channel) will once again receive notifications on v2026.6.9+. No config change needed. No restart loop.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests:

```
✓ extension-codex dynamic-tool-build.test.ts (53 tests)
  ✓ strips the internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
  ✓ preserves a real delivery channel provider
  ✓ uses the message tool channel before a differing ingress provider
  … 50 existing tests all pass
```

Live validation with the documented heartbeat scenario: the `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` unit specifies both the "webchat→undefined" regression case and the "real channel preserved" case. The outbound-policy `enforceCrossContextPolicy` behavior is unchanged — when `currentChannelProvider` is `undefined`, the provider-mismatch branch skips and the guard allows the send (matching pre-6.9 behavior).

Additional checks:

```
oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt: all matched files use the correct format
pnpm test: 53/53 passed
```

## What was not tested

Full end-to-end heartbeat → Discord roundtrip (requires live credentials). The unit test proves the channel-binding decision; live delivery behavior is unchanged from v2026.6.8 where the identical `currentChannelProvider=undefined` path was the shipping behavior.

target.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers
target.body:
## Problem

`sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` only work within a single gateway. In multi-machine setups (agents split across MacBook, iMac, Mac Studio — each running their own OpenClaw gateway), there's no native way for agents to communicate cross-gateway. The current workaround is SSH scripts (`msg-jarvis`), which are fragile and bypass all gateway auth/routing.

## Solution

Add cross-gateway routing to session tools via three complementary mechanisms:

### 1. `gateway.peers` config map (new)

Named peer gateways so agents can target remote gateways by name instead of raw URLs:

```yaml
gateway:
  peers:
    imac:
      url: wss://imac.local:18789
      token: \${env:IMAC_GATEWAY_TOKEN}
    studio:
      url: wss://studio.local:18789
```

Peer tokens support SecretInput (env refs, secret stores, plaintext).

### 2. `sessions_send`: `gateway` / `gatewayUrl` / `gatewayToken` params

```
sessions_send(sessionKey="agent:jarvis:main", message="hello", gateway="imac")
sessions_send(sessionKey="agent:pepper:main", message="hi", gatewayUrl="wss://custom:18789", gatewayToken="tok")
```

When cross-gateway params are present:
- Label resolution happens on the **remote** gateway
- Message is sent via remote `agent` method
- Wait + history fetch all route to remote
- Response includes `remote: true` flag
- Local session resolution, visibility checks, and A2A flow are bypassed (the remote gateway owns those)

### 3. `sessions_spawn`: same params

```
sessions_spawn(task="run tests", agentId="pepper", gateway="studio")
```

Forwards spawn as an agent message to the remote gateway.

### Shared helper: `gateway-peer.ts`

Resolves cross-gateway targeting from tool params:
1. `gateway: "peerName"` → looks up `gateway.peers[peerName]`
2. `gatewayUrl` + optional `gatewayToken` → explicit URL override  
3. Neither → local gateway (returns undefined, no behavior change)

Peer names take precedence when both `gateway` and `gatewayUrl` are provided.

### Design notes

- **Zero breaking changes** — local path is completely unchanged
- **Pattern already exists** — `message`, `cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`, `canvas` tools already accept `gatewayUrl`/`gatewayToken`; this extends the pattern to session tools
- **Security** — peer URLs are validated through existing `resolveGatewayOptions()` which enforces URL format and token resolution rules

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `config/zod-schema.ts` | `gateway.peers` record schema |
| `config/types.gateway.ts` | `GatewayPeerConfig` type |
| `config/schema.labels.ts` | Label for `gateway.peers` |
| `config/schema.help.ts` | Help text for `gateway.peers` |
| `agents/tools/gateway-peer.ts` | **New** — shared peer resolution helper |
| `agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` | Cross-gateway fast path + 3 new schema params |
| `agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts` | Cross-gateway fast path + 3 new schema params |
| `agents/tools/gateway-peer.test.ts` | **New** — 9 tests for peer resolution |

## Tests

- 9 new peer resolution tests (named peer, missing peer, explicit URL, precedence, error messages)
- 17 existing sessions tests pass
- 32 existing config schema tests pass

Closes #43605

target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "cbba82da-df18-4711-bbf3-35d44176525b",
  "sessionKey": "hook:c0add59f-0ac5-4772-8d12-f83efb7d99d3"
}
```

Live runtime logs (redacted, copied from `docker logs tide-corp`):

```
2026-05-10T13:59:43.228+00:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-05-10T14:03:45.904+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-05-10T14:03:53.994+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

**Observed result after fix:**

- Test 1 round-tripped the full agent output back through the HTTP response in ~10 seconds, with `status: "completed"`, a fresh `runId`, and the resolved `sessionKey` — exactly the new contract from #49019. target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909).

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → reply delivered normally

## Evidence

### 1. Second message recovers from conflict and emits reply (same session)

`e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` calls `initSessionState` twice on the identical `sessionKey`. Between turns, forced CAS conflicts simulate Codex harness activity modifying the session identity. The second message hits repeated conflicts, self-heal recovers, and the reply is delivered:

```
  ✓ Message 1: reply delivered normally (no error)

═══ BETWEEN TURNS: concurrent activity ═══
  Codex harness writes transcript mirror...
  Heartbeat updates context tracking...
  → sessionFile field changed in store

═══ MESSAGE 2: second message in SAME session ═══
  → initSessionState() loads snapshot
  → commitReplySessionInitialization: CAS begins...

    [CAS commit #2] REJECTED — revision mismatch (4 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #3] REJECTED — revision mismatch (3 forced remaining)
          ↑ SELF-HEAL TRIGGERS: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [CAS commit #4] REJECTED — revision mismatch (2 forced remaining)
    [CAS commit #5] REJECTED — revision mismatch (1 forced remaining)
          ↑ FENCED REVALIDATION: drain foreign turn + teardown + retry
```

### 2. Real CAS conflict — zero mocks

Directly calls `commitReplySessionInitialization` with stale revisions from concurrent session identity modifications. No `vi.mock`:

```

  ⚡ PRE-FIX: would throw "reply session initialization conflicted"
  ⚡ POST-FIX: self-heal triggers → dispose runtime + harness reset → retry
```

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh current-user input or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Native Codex app-server hosts now project that lane into Codex `turn/start.additionalContext` with `kind: "untrusted"`, so Codex owns the lower-authority external-fragment rendering instead of OpenClaw splicing the data into `turn/start.input`.

Embedded OpenClaw runs no longer advertise `reference-context`; they still support `assemble-before-prompt`, but engines that require a true reference-context lane are rejected there until embedded has an equivalent non-message transport.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can return historical/reference data separately from executable model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because native Codex receives the reference data through its dedicated additional-context protocol lane while chat-only/current-user prompt text stays focused on the current request.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof from a redacted local OpenClaw `runCodexAppServerAttempt` test using a fake app-server client that captures the outgoing `turn/start` params:

```text
turn/start.input contains current request: true
turn/start.input contains OpenClaw reference context: false
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.kind: untrusted
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.value contains reference summary: true
```

Real Codex app-server proof using installed `@openai/codex` 0.142.4, `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and a local mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
responseRequestCount: 1
model request contains current prompt "inspect tab": true
model request contains external reference fragment: true
external fragment:
<external_openclaw_reference_context>OpenClaw reference context for this turn:
- Reference note: browser tab title is Example Domain.</external_openclaw_reference_context>

model input item summary:
- developer instructions item
- AGENTS/environment context item
- separate user item with <external_openclaw_reference_context>...</external_openclaw_reference_context>
- separate current user item: inspect tab
```

Additional real Codex app-server clear/replace proof with the same installed app-server and mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
turn 1 additionalContext value: Reference A
turn 1 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn

turn 2 additionalContext value: Reference B
turn 2 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn

turn 3 additionalContext omitted
turn 3 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn, third turn no reference
thirdTurnHasNewExternalImmediatelyBeforePrompt: false
```

That matches Codex core behavior: `AdditionalContextStore::merge(values)` replaces the retained map with the current turn's map, and omitted app-server `additionalContext` maps to an empty map. Prior external fragments remain only as ordinary earlier transcript history; no fresh `openclaw_reference_context` fragment is injected before the current prompt when OpenClaw omits reference context.

Codex source contract checked locally in sibling `../codex`:

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs` defines experimental `turn/start.additionalContext` as camelCase `additionalContext`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs` maps omitted `additionalContext` to an empty core map.
- `codex-rs/core/src/state/additional_context.rs` replaces the retained additional-context map on each turn.
- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/additional_context.rs` renders untrusted entries as `<external_{key}>...</external_{key}>` fragments.
- `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_start.rs` covers `turn_start_additional_context_flows_to_model_input`.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/additional_context.rs` covers replacement/removal behavior and additional context being model-visible without becoming the current user turn item.

target.title: fix(codex): route internal heartbeat sends through provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server heartbeat/internal turns could be stamped as `webchat`-bound, causing Discord notification sends from those internal turns to be rejected by the default cross-provider outbound policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex message-tool routing should still prefer the explicit message channel for normal deliverable turns, but the internal `webchat` channel is only a non-delivery source marker for heartbeat-style turns. When Codex receives both `messageChannel: "webchat"` and a deliverable `messageProvider`, this change binds message-tool execution to the deliverable provider instead of the internal marker.

## User Impact

Codex-backed heartbeat notifications can send to the intended provider without requiring users to loosen cross-provider messaging settings globally.

target.title: fix(ssh-tunnel): log stderr stream errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The stderr stream error handler on the SSH child process (`startSshPortForward`) was an empty function `() => {}`, silently discarding all pipe/stream errors. While this prevented uncaught exceptions (the original intent), it made debugging tunnel failures impossible when the diagnostic pipe itself failed — operators had no visibility into why `ssh` stderr broke.

## Changes

**`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts`** (+6 −1):
- Import `createSubsystemLogger` from `../logging/subsystem.js`
- Create module-level logger: `const log = createSubsystemLogger("ssh-tunnel")`
- Replace empty error handler with `log.debug("SSH tunnel stderr stream error: %s", formatErrorMessage(err))`

**`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`** (+18 −2):
- Add `logDebug` spy to the hoisted mock set
- Mock `../logging/subsystem.js` to capture log calls
- Update the stderr error test: verify `logDebug` is called with the correct error message
- Rename test from "does not crash" → "logs stderr stream errors without crashing"

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, a persisted aborted main session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once rapid accepted recovery attempts show that the session needs operator inspection.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, which keeps the gateway focused on the same stuck session instead of leaving the row in a terminal state for inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR and makes main-session restart recovery use the same accepted-attempt fuse style as subagent recovery:

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` state with `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Reuses the shared `restart-recovery-fuse` helper so main-session and subagent automatic recovery evaluate the same rapid re-wedge pattern.
- Reserves the durable fuse before dispatching the gateway recovery run, then replaces the provisional idempotency key with the accepted run id.
- Rolls back the provisional fuse reservation when gateway dispatch fails before acceptance.
- Records the accepted recovery run id in `restartRecoveryRuns` for lifecycle suppression, while using `mainRestartRecovery` as the primary retry fuse.
- Keeps a legacy marker-derived attempt floor for old rows that already contain `restartRecoveryRuns` but do not yet have `mainRestartRecovery`.
- Accepted recovery run completion now persists its terminal lifecycle patch even when older recovery markers remain, so marker accounting does not leave a successfully recovered session looking `running`.
- Exhausted rows are tombstoned before another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and transition the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- When an exhausted row still has a restart-recovery delivery route, the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice is sent before the row is tombstoned.
- Transcript preflight/read failures do not create durable recovery state, and pre-acceptance gateway dispatch failures roll back provisional reservations.
- Existing subagent recovery state remains owned by subagent recovery; ordinary main/session progress clears stale main restart-recovery state but does not clear `subagentRecovery`.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is not the durable cross-boot policy.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- This adds only an optional internal `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` persistence field for main restart recovery. It does not add public config, wire protocol, credentials/auth behavior, provider discovery behavior, or Telegram/systemd runtime behavior.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle-suppression and legacy-floor state; it is no longer the primary retry fuse for newly accepted recoveries.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime coverage through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session that rapidly re-wedges after two accepted automatic recovery dispatches is tombstoned before a third automatic resume, while deterministic transcript failures and gateway dispatch failures before acceptance do not consume the durable attempt budget.

After inspection, normal main-session progress can clear stale main restart-recovery metadata without erasing independent subagent recovery tombstones.

## Evidence

Issue-specific runtime coverage through the production main-session restart-recovery entrypoint:

```text
Validation `tombstone-notice-regression-green` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
Covered: exhausted restart-aborted rows with a restart-recovery delivery route send the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice, skip another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and tombstone the session as `failed`.

Validation `main-restart-recovery-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
Covered: startup-orphaned main sessions record accepted attempts in mainRestartRecovery, accepted dispatches persist a provisional durable fuse before the gateway side effect, tombstone before a third rapid accepted resume, preserve accepted run markers for lifecycle suppression, apply the legacy restartRecoveryRuns floor for old rows, roll back pre-acceptance dispatch failures, and avoid charging preflight/read failures.
```

Lifecycle marker boundary:

```text
Validation `lifecycle-recovery-marker-terminal` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts
Covered: accepted recovery run completion persists terminal lifecycle state even when another recovery marker remains.
```

Touched cleanup and owner-boundary consumers:

```text
Validation `gateway-agent-recovery-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts

Validation `agent-command-recovery-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts

Validation `store-normalization-main-fuse-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/config/sessions/store.session-key-normalization.test.ts

Validation `command-session-store-main-fuse-cleanup` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts

Validation `plugin-session-entry-slot-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/plugins/contracts/session-entry-projection.contract.test.ts
```

Static/type coverage:

```text
Validation `tsgo-core-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:core

Validation `tsgo-test-precharged-main-fuse` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:test
```

Review finding disposition:

- Durable stop condition: main-session restart recovery now persists timestamped accepted-attempt fuse state in `mainRestartRecovery` and evaluates the same two-minute rapid re-wedge window style as subagent recovery.
- Accepted-dispatch charging: recovery dispatch first persists a provisional durable attempt keyed by the idempotency key, successful acceptance replaces it with the accepted run id and lifecycle marker, and failures before acceptance roll the reservation back.
- Startup-orphan budget: startup-orphaned rows no longer need synthetic initial markers; accepted recovery dispatches carry the durable attempt count across gateway boots.
- Legacy rows: old rows with only `restartRecoveryRuns` still get a conservative legacy floor so existing exhausted rows are not allowed to loop indefinitely.
- Accepted recovery lifecycle: accepted recovery run completion persists the terminal lifecycle patch while clearing recovery markers, instead of suppressing the terminal patch because another marker remains.
- Tombstone lifecycle: exhausted rows transition to `failed`, clear `abortedLastRun`, stamp terminal timing fields, and send the existing best-effort notice when a restart-recovery delivery route exists before another resume dispatch.
- Subagent boundary: subagent recovery keeps its existing persisted owner state; main-session recovery and ordinary main/session progress do not write or clear it.
- Normal progress cleanup: ordinary user progress clears stale main restart-recovery flags through the existing cleanup path.

target.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a bug where `openclaw agents add --bind 'feishu:oc_test'` generated bindings with `accountId` format instead of `peer` format, causing messages to route to the default agent instead of the intended agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The routing engine matches conversations using the `peer` field for channel-specific routing (like feishu group chats), but `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` were generating `accountId` format by default.

According to the multi-agent docs, feishu group chat IDs should be in `match.peer: { kind: "group", id: "..." }` format, not `match.accountId`.

## User Impact

- **Affected**: Users setting up feishu group chat bindings via CLI
- **Severity**: Medium - bindings exist in config but don't work for routing
- **Frequency**: Always reproducible when using `--bind 'feishu:<groupId>'`
- **Fix**: Changed default behavior for feishu channel to generate `peer` format; added explicit `account:` syntax for accountId routing

## Evidence

### Before Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "oc_test" }
}
# Result: Messages route to default agent (main)
```

### After Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "peer": { "kind": "group", "id": "oc_test" } }
}
# Result: Messages correctly route to feishu-agent
```

### Explicit AccountId Syntax
For multi-account feishu setups, use the explicit syntax:
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:account:work'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "work" }
}
```

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive tests in `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts`:
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu group binding as peer format
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu explicit accountId syntax
- parseBindingSpecs: reject invalid binding with too many colons
- parseBindingSpecs: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)
- buildChannelBindings: feishu group binding as peer format
- buildChannelBindings: feishu explicit accountId binding
- buildChannelBindings: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)

All 7 tests pass.

## Files Changed

- `src/commands/agents.bindings.ts` - Modified `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` to support peer format for feishu
- `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts` - Added tests for new binding formats

Closes #95734

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(gateway): hot-reload acp config instead of restarting gateway
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102205 — adding `acp` config to `openclaw.json` triggers an infinite
gateway restart loop: gateway auto-enables acpx, detects the acp key as a
config change requiring restart, restarts, and repeats.

## Root Cause

`src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` has no reload rule for the `acp` top-level
config key. When `acp` is added or changed, `matchRule("acp")` returns null,
defaulting to `kind: "restart"`. This triggers a full gateway restart even
though acpx runtime can be hot-reloaded via `reload-plugins`.

## Fix

Add `{ prefix: "acp", kind: "hot", actions: ["reload-plugins"] }` to
`BASE_RELOAD_RULES_TAIL`. ACP config changes now hot-reload plugins instead of
restarting the gateway.

1 line in `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts`.

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof — production gateway

**Before (main `4bf70be01a`):**

ACP config change triggers restart loop:

```
config change detected; evaluating reload (…acp)
config change requires gateway restart (acp)
http server listening (14 plugins: acpx, …)    ← first start ok
[restart]
http server listening (13 plugins: …)          ← acpx gone after self-restart
config change detected; evaluating reload (…acp)  ← detects again
config change requires gateway restart (acp)   ← loops forever
```

**After (this PR):**

Same ACP config. Gateway stable with acpx loaded, no self-triggered restart:

```
embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily
http server listening (14 plugins: acpx, …)    ← acpx loaded, stable
```

Gateway has been stable for 30+ minutes. No "config change requires gateway
restart" since deploying the fix.

### Regression Test

Added 2 tests in `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts`:
- `"hot-reloads plugins for acp config changes instead of restarting"` —
  verifies `acp.enabled` changes are hot-reloaded with `reloadPlugins: true`
- `"hot-reloads plugins for acp.backend config changes"` — same for
  `acp.backend`

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)  Tests  356 passed (356)
```

- [x] oxfmt + oxlint pass
- [x] git diff --check pass
- [x] Production gateway stable with acpx loaded (14 plugins)

target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json   -> clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>                        -> clean
oxfmt --check <7 changed files>                                      -> clean
```

New tests in this revision (`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts`):

- `recomputes runtime-config drift on cache hits so read-scoped callers see fresh drift` -- cached "ok" + drift recompute -> `operator.read` cache hit (`{ cached: true }` respond flag asserted) returns `state: "drift"` with no fingerprints.
- `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute so fingerprints stay admin-only` -- same cache-hit path with `operator.admin` receives fingerprints; background refresh still runs.
- `drops a stale cached runtime-config summary when the recompute returns none`.

Live behavior proof (redacted, exact head): see the `Real behavior proof` section below -- a sandbox gateway built from this head shows the ok -> drift transition on the plain, non-verbose, read-scoped `openclaw health` path after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `mode: "hot"`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: plain `openclaw health` (least-privilege `operator.read`, both JSON and text) reports `runtimeConfig.state: "drift"` with `driftPaths: ["gateway.auth"]` after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"`, including when the response is served from the 60s health cache; fingerprints are omitted for read-scoped callers.

Real environment tested: sandbox gateway on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), dist built from this branch at head `4229b9999d` content, launched with `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 28934`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config: `gateway.mode: "local"`, `gateway.auth: { mode: "token", token: "sandbox-token-OLD" }`, `gateway.reload: { mode: "hot", debounceMs: 100 }`, `agents.defaults.model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node dist/index.js health --json                 # call 1, fills the health cache
sed -i.bak 's/sandbox-token-OLD/sandbox-token-NEW/' $SANDBOX/openclaw.json
sleep 4
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health --json   # call 2, ~40s after call 1
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health          # text mode
```

Evidence after fix:

- Call 1 (before rotation): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "ok", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5"}` -- no fingerprint fields on the read-scoped path.
- Gateway reload log after `sed`:
  ```
  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.token)
  [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.auth.token)
  ```
- Call 2 (after rotation, inside the 60s `HEALTH_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` window of call 1, i.e. the cache-hit merge path): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "drift", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "driftPaths": ["gateway.auth"], "message": "Live gateway runtime config differs from disk for model/provider/auth paths; restart is required or pending."}` -- no fingerprint fields.
- Text mode: `Runtime config: warning (live gateway differs from disk for gateway.auth; restart required or pending; live=openai/gpt-5.5 disk=openai/gpt-5.5)`.

Observed result after fix: the ok -> drift transition is visible on the normal read-scoped `openclaw health` path immediately after the disk change, with hot mode still warn-and-keep (live gateway kept accepting `sandbox-token-OLD`); the earlier caveat about the in-process snapshot-refresh handler masking external edits no longer reproduces on current main.

What was not tested: admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) live output with fingerprints (covered by unit tests `surfaces model/provider runtime config drift ... in sensitive snapshots` and `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute`); live drift on the non-auth tracked paths such as `agents.defaults.model` or `auth.profiles` (covered by unit tests); the `{ cached: true }` respond flag is not printed by the CLI, so cache-hit routing of call 2 is established by the 60s window timing plus the deterministic handler tests.

## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. target.title: Fix/hooks agent accountid normalization
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: `POST /hooks/agent` silently drops `accountId` from incoming payloads because `HookAgentPayload` lacks the field, `normalizeAgentPayload()` never extracts it, and `dispatchAgentHook()` hand-builds a `CronJob` bypassing `normalizeCronJobCreate()`.
- Why it matters: Multi-account WhatsApp (and any channel requiring `accountId`) delivery fails silently — the caller gets a success response but the message is never sent.
- What changed: Hook dispatch now routes through `normalizeCronJobCreate()`, which promotes legacy flat fields into proper `CronDelivery` with `accountId`. `resolveCronToolPolicy()` derives `disableMessageTool` for shared-contract callers from whether the target is fully resolved (explicit mode + accountId) instead of unconditionally disabling.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): The cron-owned path (`deliveryContract: "cron-owned"`) is untouched. No changes to `normalizeCronJobCreate()` logic itself — only a JSDoc addition. No new config options or API surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #43866
- Related #27015, #24186, #42244, #23853, #16925, #30052, #29090

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `POST /hooks/agent` now correctly preserves `accountId` through to delivery, enabling multi-account WhatsApp delivery via hooks.
- For shared-contract hook runs with a fully resolved delivery target (explicit mode + accountId), the agent's message tool is no longer unconditionally disabled — it remains available as a fallback. The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) prevents duplicate sends.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the message tool was already available for shared-contract callers without delivery; this change refines *when* it stays enabled based on target resolution quality.
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: All (server-side code path)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any (not model/provider-specific)
- Integration/channel (if any): WhatsApp (any multi-account channel)
- Relevant config (redacted): Hooks enabled with token, WhatsApp channel configured with multiple `accountId` connections

### Steps

1. Configure two WhatsApp connections with distinct `accountId` values.
2. Send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{ "message": "Hello", "channel": "whatsapp", "to": "1234567890", "accountId": "botnumber" }`.
3. Observe delivery result.

### Expected

- `accountId` flows through to `CronDelivery.accountId`, `resolveDeliveryTarget()` identifies the correct WhatsApp connection, and the message is delivered.

### Actual (before fix)

- `accountId` is silently dropped. Delivery fails because no connection can be identified. Caller receives success response.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

New tests added in second commit:
- `src/gateway/hooks.test.ts` — `normalizeAgentPayload` extracts and trims `accountId` (present, absent, blank)
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` — integration test: `accountId` propagates into `job.delivery` via cron normalization pipeline
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 tests for shared-contract tool policy: fully resolved target (explicit + accountId → enabled), missing accountId (→ disabled), implicitly resolved target (→ disabled)

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` clean, `pnpm check` clean, all 59 tests across the 4 test files pass.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format (`pnpm check`), unit + integration tests pass for all modified test files
- Edge cases checked: blank/missing `accountId`, `normalizeCronJobCreate` returning null (guard added), implicit vs explicit delivery target mode, `mode: "none"` (verified `deliveryRequested` is already `false` so no extra clause needed)
- What you did **not** verify: live end-to-end delivery through a real WhatsApp multi-account setup; only verified through unit/integration tests and code tracing

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert both commits; the hand-built CronJob path is fully self-contained in the reverted `dispatchAgentHook()`.
- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/hooks.ts`, `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`, `src/cron/normalize.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Hook agent dispatches returning early with "normalizeCronJobCreate returned null" warning (would indicate the normalizer rejects a payload shape it previously accepted via hand-built path).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `normalizeCronJobCreate()` could reject a hook payload shape that the hand-built path previously accepted, causing hook dispatches to silently no-op.
  - Mitigation: A null-return guard logs a warning and still returns a `runId` to the caller. The normalizer is well-tested and accepts all fields the hook path provides. Integration test verifies the full pipeline.

- Risk: Enabling the message tool for shared-contract callers with fully resolved targets could cause duplicate sends (agent sends via tool + automatic delivery sends again).
  - Mitigation: The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) already detects when the agent's message tool sent to the same target and skips automatic delivery. This guard predates this change and is tested.

target.title: fix: stop model catalog warning loop during sidecar refresh
target.body:
Closes #99390

AI-assisted: yes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the model-catalog warning loop where generated plugin catalog sidecar writes can fail while the private fs-safe store is protecting `catalog.json`. The reported failure is `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation`; when it lands at the generated catalog write boundary, the sidecar file can remain unwritten and dynamic provider rows stay stale or unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix now covers the owner-side write boundary directly:

- `writeModelsFileAtomicForModelsJson` reopens and retries the private store once when fs-safe reports a transient directory identity swap (`path-mismatch`) or when the same replacement race surfaces as `ENOENT` / `ENOTDIR` during the write.
- Generated plugin sidecar writes and read-only persisted catalog scans for the same agent directory share the existing process-wide model catalog file I/O queue, so readers no longer observe the sidecar tree mid-refresh.

The retry remains narrow: non-transient fs-safe failures such as denied paths still fail without retry. No provider catalog schema, runtime config, plugin SDK surface, dependency, or migration shape changes.

## User Impact

Gateway model-catalog refreshes can recover when a generated plugin catalog directory is replaced during the atomic private-store write. Dynamic provider discovery should be able to publish the refreshed sidecar instead of repeatedly logging the catalog load warning while leaving provider rows stale.

## Evidence

Exact head: `99d145c75fedffff1de4373800a799e6482998e7`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts` (1 file, 3 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.write-serialization.test.ts` (1 file, 15 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-catalog.test.ts src/agents/models-config.write-serialization.test.ts src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts src/gateway/server-model-catalog.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/models.test.ts` (7 files, 111 tests)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/models-config-state.ts src/agents/models-config.ts src/agents/model-catalog.ts src/agents/models-config.write-serialization.test.ts src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 src/agents/models-config-state.ts src/agents/models-config.ts src/agents/model-catalog.ts src/agents/models-config.write-serialization.test.ts src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` reported no accepted/actionable findings.

Deterministic fs-safe boundary proof: `src/agents/models-config.file-mode.test.ts` uses the real `@openclaw/fs-safe` private `fileStore({ private: true })` write path. During the first atomic write of `plugins/zai/catalog.json`, the fs-safe test hook replaces the generated catalog directory after the pinned rename; `writeModelsFileAtomicForModelsJson` then retries and writes the catalog into the replacement directory. The companion serialization tests also verify that `path-mismatch` is retried once and non-transient `denied-path` is not retried.

Proof gap: I did not run a live authenticated Anthropic/systemd gateway reproduction. The new proof is deterministic at the private-store/fs-safe write boundary that prior maintainer review identified as the production failure source.

target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution can fall back to environment variables in some configurations; operators lacked a dedicated audit finding when that fallback was active.

**Concrete example:** An operator adds a world-writable `/tmp/demo-plugin` to `plugins.load.paths` and configures gateway auth via SecretRef that silently resolves from `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Before this PR, `openclaw security audit` did not surface either risk explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(auto-reply,agents/tools): strip foreign provider prefix in formatProviderModelRef
target.body:
## Bug

`formatProviderModelRef(provider, model)` only stripped a *matching* provider prefix. When `model` embedded a **different** provider prefix, the function returned a malformed result:

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/openai/gpt-5.4"  // WRONG
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "openai/gpt-5.4"          // OK (existing behavior)
```

This leaks a stale, malformed `provider/model` ref into the status banner / fallback transition rendering. End users saw the wrong provider label after a fallback attempt, even though the active runtime was correctly configured for the new provider.

## Impact

- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts` is the public-facing path used by status banners.
- The same bug exists in two local copies:
  - `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts:159`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts:24`

## Fix

After existing same-prefix stripping, additionally check for any single `/`-delimited embedded provider segment that does **not** match the requested provider, and strip it. Same-prefix strip is now case-insensitive on the provider comparison.

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/gpt-5.4"  // FIXED
formatProviderModelRef("OpenAI",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "OpenAI/gpt-5.4"  // case-insensitive
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "gpt-5.4")        -> "openai/gpt-5.4"  // unchanged
```

Applied to all three local copies:
- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

## Tests

12 new cases in `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.test.ts` + 6 new cases appended in each of:
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.test.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

Direct `vitest run` of all four test files (including the existing `fallback-state.test.ts` regression suite covering `buildFallbackNotice`, `resolveFallbackTransition`, etc.) reports **111/111 passing**.

Note: `pnpm test:unit` excludes `src/auto-reply/**` and `src/agents/**` from the unit shard by config (`test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts` → `unitTestAdditionalExcludePatterns`), so those files are exercised via the dedicated `vitest run` invocation above. Total unit-suite failure count on the branch is unchanged from `main` (3 pre-existing failures in `src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts`).

target.title: fix(schema): resolve large local refs in schema arrays
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where JSON Schema validators/defaulting would reject a valid local `$ref` into a large schema array when the referenced array index exceeded OpenClaw's config path sparse-write limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON Pointer array indexes and OpenClaw config path array indexes have different ownership and limits. This keeps JSON Pointer parsing local to the schema helper, preserving canonical non-negative array-token parsing without applying the config writer's `100000` sparse-write cap.

## User Impact

Plugin/config schema validation can now resolve valid local refs such as `#/prefixItems/100001` instead of reporting them as unresolved only because they are above the config path write limit.

docs(k8s) OOM-kills happen when openclaw runs its various node tools when k8s limits are set.

## What Problem This Solves

on kubernetes, OOM-kills happen when openclaw runs its various node tools when k8s limits are set.

## Why This Change Was Made

This documentation and example would have saved me the time it took to debug and discover the node setting needed to stop node from trying to gobble up more resources than allowed.

The crash is especially hard to recover from because upon automatic restart the agent goes into a blocking unresponsive state with no logging due to the gateway lock loop state the OOM-kill puts the container into - also observed in the fly fix https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/1572

## User Impact

The impact is avoiding the fatal crash that happens when the agent runs its node-based tools for purposes such as status/healthcheck.

## Evidence

1. The change in the example deployment.yaml fixed the issue for me locally.
2. Fix is modeled after the existing openclaw fly docs and examples as fly container orchestration has the same exposure to this issue and solved it specific for fly.  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/1572
- deploy/fly.private.toml:22 — NODE_OPTIONS = "--max-old-space-size=1536" (the actual config)
- docs/install/fly.md:59 — same line, in the Fly install doc
3. <EDIT> proof that making these changes fixed the OOM kills is the pods started with the fix kept running instead of immediately getting killed.  Console from today showing the pods ran for 2 days before some unrelated cluster node changes w/o incident:

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

Live testing also showed that some Feishu app configurations may not deliver `im.message.recalled_v1` to the plugin, while Feishu's message reaction API still returns code `231003` (`message not found / maybe deleted`) when the typing target is the recalled source message. The Feishu dispatcher now treats that specific channel-local signal as a conservative fallback only when the missing typing target is the inbound source message, then reuses the same recall registry, abort signal, and reply-suppression path.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped when the recall event is delivered, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall or missing-source fallback lands before delivery.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/typing.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.message-handler.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.reaction.test.ts`

target.title: fix: mark empty tool-error turns non-deliverable
target.body:
Related: #99645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. Explicit external aborts and timeouts still record interrupted, but internally aborted empty turns without delivery evidence record `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` instead of success/interrupted without a typed terminal error.

Codex contract checked: `openai/codex@ad2012d` shows command approval responses carry `decision` values in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1329`, declined command executions are rejected/approval-denied outcomes in `codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs:2262`, and malformed app-server command approval responses default to `Decline` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1963`.

## User Impact

Users and operators should no longer see an empty declined-native-tool turn recorded as a successful completed session solely because the attempt had a tool error. Real message delivery with a later tool error is still treated as terminal progress, so multi-target or partially delivered turns do not regress.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating videos from providers that return URL-only assets could have the CLI download provider-supplied URLs without applying the configured provider request network policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now resolves the selected provider's request policy for URL-only generated video assets and downloads them through the guarded provider HTTP path. This preserves streaming output and in-memory size caps while keeping provider request config as the opt-in path for private-network downloads.

## User Impact

CLI video generation keeps working for normal provider-hosted media, blocks private/internal download targets by default, and still permits configured private-network providers when operators opt into that request policy.
